id: linear-coset-shift-periodic-density-iff-separable
kind: claim
title: The linear coset shift of a finitely generated subgroup has dense periodic points iff the subgroup is separable, so periodic density for linear SFTs forces LERF
artifacts:
  - research/artifacts/primitive-shift-goodness-dictionary-2026-09-18.md
---

**Setup.** Let `G` be a group, let `K <= G` be generated by finitely many elements
`k_1, ..., k_r`, and let `B` be a finite abelian group with `|B| >= 2`. Put
`X_K := {c ∈ B^G : c(gk) = c(g) for all g ∈ G, k ∈ K}`.

1. **Structure.** `X_K` is a linear (group) shift of finite type under the left shift. It
   is cut out by the local rules `c(g k_i) = c(g)`.
2. **Density criterion.** The periodic points of `X_K`, those with finite-index
   stabilizer, are dense in `X_K` exactly when `K` is closed in the profinite topology
   of `G`.
3. **LERF.** Suppose that, on a finitely generated group `G`, every linear SFT over `F_p`
   has dense periodic points. Then `G` is LERF.

**Reading.**
- **The density principle is too strong.** Rips-construction hyperbolic groups are
  cubulated and good, yet not LERF (recalled). On them, periodic density for linear SFTs
  fails. So the principle "linear/group SFTs have dense periodic points" (Kitchens–Schmidt
  for `Z^d`; Fiorenzi, arXiv:1402.3448, Cor. 7.2, for finitely generated abelian groups)
  is strictly stronger than goodness on hyperbolic groups.
- **It cannot prove goodness at full strength.** By
  `primitive-shifts-detect-virtual-vanishing`, only the periodic points of the specific
  primitive shifts are equivalent to goodness. A symbolic proof of
  `every-hyperbolic-group-is-good` must use features of those shifts that general linear
  SFTs lack.

Derivation: `linear-coset-shift-periodic-density-iff-separable-proof`.
